subject: Post-demo: secure SDK + network architecture checklist for HelioHealth integration

Subject: Post-demo: secure SDK + network architecture checklist for HelioHealth integration

Thanks again for the demo time today, Sam — great to see the HelioHealth use cases laid out. Attached is a concise checklist we put together to capture the low-friction items we discussed and the outstanding technical questions we'll need to answer before an integration POC. (attachment: redwood-networking-checklist.pdf, 24KB)

Quick recap / ask list from our side:
- Integration mode: you mentioned preference for a private integration (no public API keys in customer traffic). Can you confirm: VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink-style) vs. customer egress to our public endpoints with IP allowlist?
- Auth: would you prefer short-lived tokens (recommended) via your Identity Provider → STS, or use static customer-managed API keys with HSM/KMS for storage?
- Routing / fallbacks: do you want traffic pinned to a dedicated pool in us-east-1, with automated fallback to hosted capacity in the same region?
- Networking specifics:
  - Are you planning to NAT all egress through a set of fixed IPs (we can provide IP ranges for allowlisting)?
  - DNS resolution: will you want to resolve our private endpoint via customer DNS (split-horizon) or use our mTLS-enabled ingress?
- mTLS: you asked about mutual TLS — we support mTLS to authenticate client apps at the TLS layer; we'll need the certs/CA details or to generate a client cert per-connector.
- Embeddings / reranker flow: recommended pattern is to send embeddings through a dedicated embeddings endpoint with affinity to the same region as your index. If you plan to perform reranking server-side, we should review tokenization and latency SLOs for 1–2s p50.

Next steps proposed:
1) Please share the security contact (name + email) so we can get them the standard questionnaire and our SOC2 + network diagrams.
2) Karthik (SE) will draft an SDK auth flow and an egress diagram for your infra team.
3) Let's schedule a 30-minute architecture call with your security and network teams to lock down the VPC/DNS/mTLS approach.

Thanks — I attached the checklist to make it easier for your infra team.

—
Monica Patel

On Mon, Jul 12, 2026 at 3:04 PM Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo time today, Sam — great to see the HelioHealth use cases laid out. Attached is a concise checklist...

Thanks, Monica — super helpful checklist. Answers inline below: 
- Integration mode: we prefer a PrivateLink-style VPC endpoint if Redwood supports that in AWS (Helio infra is in AWS). If not feasible, we can do egress to Redwood public endpoints and maintain NATed static IPs for allowlisting.
- Auth: prefer short-lived tokens obtained from our IdP (Okta). We'll push for token exchange / STS flow rather than storing long-lived API keys.
- Routing / fallbacks: yes, pin to a dedicated pool in us-east-1. Failover to hosted in the same region is acceptable.
- Networking specifics:
  - Egress: we plan to NAT through a small set of static IPs — I'll confirm the exact addresses with networking.
  - DNS: we'd prefer to resolve an internal hostname (split-horizon) that maps to the PrivateLink endpoint.
- mTLS: we want mTLS for client auth to the endpoint. I'll loop in Alicia (security lead) for cert management.
- Embeddings / reranker: we'll run embedding generation in batch from our ETL job and use the Redwood embeddings endpoint. Reranking will be server-side; latency target is p95 < 2s for interactive queries.

Attaching our security questionnaire — Alicia will be able to add details. (attachment: helio-security-questionnaire.pdf, 120KB)

Alicia — can you confirm whether Helio can provide a CA bundle for mTLS or if you'd prefer Redwood to issue client certs per connector?

Thanks,
Sam

Thanks for the details, Sam — appreciate the clarity. A few technical notes and what we'll provide ahead of the architecture sync: 

SDK / Auth options (recommended order):
1) Short-lived token flow via STS: Helio exchanges an Okta-signed assertion for a short-lived Redwood token (recommended). This minimizes long-lived secrets on your side. We'll provide an example flow (OAuth token exchange + STS) and an SDK helper that refreshes tokens automatically.
2) mTLS + client cert: if you want TLS-layer mutual auth, we can require client certs for the PrivateLink endpoint. Certs can be customer-supplied (you manage CA) or we can issue certs per connector and rotate them.
3) Static API key (least preferred): supported, stored encrypted (KMS), but not our recommendation for production.

Networking / Private endpoint details:
- PrivateLink: we support AWS Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink) for dedicated pools. That will give you a private ENI in your VPC and DNS entries you can resolve internally.
- IP allowlist: if you prefer egress to public endpoints, we can provide a small set of egress IP prefixes per region.
- DNS: for PrivateLink we recommend using split-horizon DNS — we'll share the CNAMEs and records you should add.
- mTLS: we can do client cert validation at our edge and perform cert revocation checks. If Helio manages the CA, we will accept your CA bundle and verify client certs against it.

Embedding / Reranker guidance:
- Embeddings endpoint: send dense vectors to the embeddings endpoint in us-east-1. For high-throughput bulk ETL, use our batch ingest API (multipart upload + async index job).
- Reranker: serve reranker calls from a dedicated route pinned to the same pool as the embeddings to avoid cross-region token hopping and to hit lower tokenization variance. Typical tokens-per-rerank call ~300–700 depending on context.

Attachments I will drop in the shared folder prior to the call:
- sdk-auth-flow.drawio (sequence diagram for token exchange / certificate flow)
- network-egress-sample.yaml (sample NAT/egress config)

Proposed pre-call deliverables from Redwood:
- Sequence diagram for STS token exchange and SDK snippet
- PrivateLink DNS/CNAME details and cert acceptance checklist
- List of egress IP prefixes for us-east-1 (if you go that route)

I can take the technical lead on the sync; Monica, can you propose two slots tomorrow or Thursday morning PT?

—
Karthik Iyer
